description: "Comparison of pairwise statements in a strict ranking and KRW's report cards for 97 firms."
---

Kline, Rose and Walters (2024) estimated race and gender contact gaps for 97 large U.S. employers. A strict ranking orders all 4,656 firm pairs. KRW’s cards order firms in different grades, including some pairs whose direction is uncertain.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Race card.** Asserting all 4,656 pairs gives wrong share .300; KRW's card states 1,324 (.284, wrong share .136; 1,219 agree, 105 reverse) and withholds 3,332.
- **Second place.** Nationwide (.402 ± .216) shares grade 2 with 80 other firms: 16 of 96 pairs stated (15 agree, 1 reverse).
- **Last place.** State Farm (−.544 ± .444) shrinks to rank 14 by posterior mean (.155): 16 stated (2 agree, 14 reverse; [shrinkage](shrinkage.qmd)).
- **By posterior mean.** Genuine Parts leads (.250; estimate .330 ± .0714), and all 1,324 stated pairs agree.
- **Gender card.** Four grades (sizes 1, 3, 89, 4) state 731 pairs (.157, wrong share .115; 730 agree, 1 reverses); Builders FirstSource states all 96.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Sources: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figures 7 and 14 and slides 4–5, 61–63, doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC, noncommercial use only, adapted in `pr_case_krw`. Grade 1 is ★; shared grades mean not compared. Provided as is, no endorsement implied; **the data describe KRW's experiment, not current conduct.**
:::

library(postrank)
pr_case_krw$reference$single_criterion$archive_metrics[, c("criterion", "grade_sizes", "N", "M", "s")]  # race 2/81/14: 1324 of 4656; gender 1/3/89/4: 731
head(pr_case_krw$units[order(-pr_case_krw$units$race_estimate), c("firm_name", "race_estimate", "race_se")], 2)  # AutoNation 0.4332195, Nationwide 0.4022631
